scenes.name: Edimburgo: Josef K y The Fire Engines
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Bibliófilos postpunk del pub The Tap of Lauriston. Josef K (Paul Haig, Malcolm Ross), con pilotos grises, guitarras «tintineantes» sin distorsión a lo Television y Talking Heads 77, punk disco más áspero que Orange Juice y letras sobre Kafka, Camus y Hamsun: «Sorry for Laughing», «It's Kinda Funny» (por la muerte de Curtis), «Endless Soul». Su único álbum, The Only Fun in Town (1981), regrabado para sonar en vivo, decepcionó y sembró el indie de guitarras agresivas de los ochenta. The Fire Engines, conciertos de quince minutos y funk esquizoide a lo Subway Sect, Beefheart y Contortions: Lubricate Your Living Room (1981), «música de fondo para gente activa» editada por Bob Last en Pop: Aural; después serán Win.

podcast.title: Formation and Early Success
podcast.body: The Skids, an important early Scottish Celtic punk band from Dunfermline, formed in 1977 when Stuart Adamson assembled a group of friends. They released several strong singles between 1978 and 1979, with one reaching the top 10 of the UK singles chart. "They came together in 1977 when Stuart Adamson roped together a bunch of friends. The Skids ended up having several strong singles out of the gate through 1978 and 1979. One of them reached into the top 10 of the UK singles chart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Projects
podcast.body: The group disbanded in 1982, leading its members in different directions. Guitarist Stuart Adamson went on to form Big Country, one of the most successful Scottish bands of the 1980s. "The group lasted until 1982 when they cleaved in several different directions. Guitarist Stuart Adamson's next project was Big Country, one of the most successful Scottish bands of the 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunions
podcast.body: The Skids reformed for a three-year period following a reunion in 2007, and another reunion initiated in 2016 has remained active. Stuart Adamson was not part of these reunions. "Meanwhile the Skids reformed for three years following a reunion in 2007. And another reunion in 2016 has stuck."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Solo Career Trajectory
xref.body: After The Smiths' breakup, Morrissey initially seemed poised to become a major solo star, benefiting from the cult following he amassed with his previous band. However, his solo career began to decline in the mid-1990s, as he struggled to produce consistent albums, moved to Los Angeles, refused interviews, and toured less frequently. "Although it got off to a promising start, Morris' solo career hit the skids in the mid 1990s."
